findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: The person in charge (PIC) could not show proof of his food manager certificate. Ensure that every person that handles food and clean dishes obtains a food manager certificate and be sure that certificates are made available for all routine inspections.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Required records available: molluscan shellfish identification, and parasite destruction.
findings.comment: The facility could not produce a letter of guarantee form for their sushi supplier. Discussed with the PIC that the purpose of the form is to certify that the raw fish supplier complies with food safety laws and has followed the proper procedures to remove parasites. Ensure that letter of guarantee forms are current per calendar year and are available for routine inspections. Will follow-up September 2, 2026 to see that form is available.
findings.citation_text: 3-402.11(A) Parasite Destruction. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, before service or sale in READY TO-EAT form, raw, raw-marinated, partially cooked, or marinated-partially cooked FISH shall be: (1) Frozen and stored at a temperature of -20°C (-4°F) or below for a minimum of 168 hours (7 days) in a freezer; (2) Frozen at -35°C (-31°F) or below until solid and stored at -35°C (-31°F) or below for a minimum of 15 hours; or (3) Frozen at -35°C (-31°F) or below until solid and stored at -20°C (-4°F) or below for a minimum of 24 hours.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
findings.comment:
There has been a history of falsifying pH logs for the acidified sushi rice. See violation #29 for further details. The PIC has continuously falsified data logged within record logs.This violation alone will warrant a number of additional spot checks to ensure staff is properly trained and understands the importance of monitoring and logging. 

PIC has not demonstrated knowledge of food safety practices. PIC has continued to operate without essential equipment (pH meter) or other interim measures in place. Operator was noted to have falsified data logged within record logs. This violation alone will warrant a number of additional spot checks to insure staff is properly trained and understands the importance of monitoring and logging. See violations below.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.11(A) Demonstration. Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, during inspections and upon request the PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the HAZARD Analysis and CRITICAL CONTROL POINT principles, and the requirements of this Code. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate this knowledge by: (A) Complying with this Code by having no violations of PRIORITY ITEMS during the current inspection. [Pf]

findings.title: Compliance with variance/specialized process/HACCP.
findings.comment:
It is evident that the PIC is falsifying pH records. The PIC noted two pH recordings, however, one of the recordings had been pre written for a future time (9:59am). Discussed with the PIC that falsifying records is against the facility’s HACCP Plan and also inaccurate record keeping. Ensure that pH records are accurate and never falsified. Will follow-up on April 6, 2026 to ensure that records are being correctly monitored by the PIC. 

Logs and discussion with the PIC indicate sushi rice pH and pH meter logs have been falsified. Logs reflect that the pH meter has been calibrated and sushi pH measured over the last week despite the lack of a functional pH meter in the facility. Staff must record accurate HACCP records. Inspector will follow up to see that accurate logs are maintained.
findings.citation_text: 8-103.12(C) Conformance with Approved Procedures. If the REGULATORY AUTHORITY grants a VARIANCE as specified in § 8-103.10, or a HACCP PLAN is otherwise required as specified under § 8-201.13, the PERMIT HOLDER shall: (C) Maintain and provide to the regulatory authority, upon request, records specified under § 8-201.14 (D) and (E)(3) that demonstrate that the following are routinely employed; (1) Procedures for monitoring the CRITICAL CONTROL POINTS, (2) Monitoring of the CRITICAL CONTROL POINTS, (3) Verification of the effectiveness of the operation or process, and (4) Necessary corrective actions if there is failure at a CRITICAL CONTROL POINT.

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records.
findings.comment: Sushi rice is not acidified, nor is a Time as a Control policy in place to maintain food safety while rice is held on the countertop to make sushi rolls. Discussed the use of Time as a Control with PIC. If sushi rice used from cooking, rolls created from that rice need to be created and sold within 4 hours of rice being removed from the rice cooker. If sushi rice is cooled to 41F within 6 hours (and logs are maintained), sushi rolls created from that rice need to be sold within 6 hours of the rice being removed from cold-holding. Sushi packages need to be labeled to indicate the time that they should be consumed by.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.19(B)(3) Time as a Public Health Control. (B) If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 4 hours: (3) The FOOD shall be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the FOOD is removed from temperature control. [Pf]

findings.title: Compliance with variance/specialized process/HACCP.
findings.comment: Facility does not have a functional pH meter. The pH meter was not functional during the previous inspection. PIC indicated during this inspection that the pH meter has not been used since the previous inspection. Facility must have functional equipment to measure sushi rice pH and use it regularly. PIC has ordered a new pH meter. Inspector will follow up to see that a new pH meter is provided and verify PIC’s ability to use said meter.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
PIC was observed touching face and other surfaces before donning gloves to engage in food preparation. Hand washing did not occur before between activities. The activity was ceased and PIC was instructed to wash hands before putting on a fresh pair of gloves. Ensure that hand washing occurs before donning gloves if task changes. 

2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed several TCS foods stored in the reach-in cooler to not be date marked. These items include but are not limited to imitation crab, chicken, shrimp, and homemade sauce. Discussed with PIC that items should be date marked if stored in house for longer than 24 hours. Ensure that TCS food is date marked if stored in house longer than 24 hours and discarded if not used within 7 days. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).
